data.body:
RP-06 D6.2 research complete: `.joe-janitor/rp06-empty-applies-to.md`. Under approved effective applicability, empty project code-review `applies_to` is ambiguous: built-ins already use `[]` for escalation-only, content-triggered, base/posture-only, and detector-wide cases, while the one active project LLM criterion historically used it for unconditional Round-A fan-in. Current overlay validation does not validate `applies_to`; the RP-06 probe proves even `["src/**"]` is currently ignored on a docs-only diff.

Recommendation: for net-new `project.*` code-review LLM entries only, require a non-empty list of non-empty repo-relative globs; `["**"]` explicitly means repository-wide. Match any changed path -> execute exactly once in Round A; no match -> typed skipped/non-applicable provenance. Fail loudly at overlay/editor validation with a `["**"]` remedy. Migrate this repo's `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]`, preserving its intentional all-review behavior. Packaged built-ins retain their secondary-trigger semantics; project DET remains detector-selected; plan-review keeps `applies_at`/`trigger`. Actual `glob_match` probe confirms `**` matches root, nested, and dot paths, while `**/*` misses root files. GitHub Actions and ESLint prior art favor visible path selection/global applicability rather than an overloaded empty selector. Maintainer approval pending.
